slides.headline: Senegal have their Africa Cup title back. Here’s why
slides.subline: **A court just reversed** one of football’s strangest rulings.

slides.body: In the **January final** against Morocco, Senegal’s players walked off in protest at a late penalty. Play restarted, Morocco’s penalty was saved, and Senegal won [[1-0]] in extra time.
In March, African football’s governing body, **CAF**, ruled the walk-off a forfeit. It handed Morocco the title with a [[3-0]] result on paper.
On **Nov 24** the Court of Arbitration for Sport set that aside. Its panel said the referee **restarted the match**, so the forfeit rules did not apply. The [[1-0]] stands.
Senegal’s federation called it “justice for sport”. **Morocco** disputed the verdict and vowed to use [[all legal avenues]]. CAF said it accepts the ruling.
Morocco’s challenge is still pending, so the story may not be over. Should a match result ever be decided in a courtroom? Tell us below.
